texts.preamble: R. Nikhil vs The State Of Telengana Rep. By Its ... on 26 December, 2022 Author: Lalitha Kanneganti Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti Writ Petition No. 5794 Of 2016 O R D E R:
texts.facts: This Writ Petition is filed seeking the following relief: " .... to issue a writ, order or direction more in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ declaring the action of the respondents herein banning and interfering with the business of the petitioner in serving of favoured hookahs without reference to any rule, law or regulations as illegal, arbitrary, contrary to the provisions of the Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 and consequently, direct the respondents to permit the petitioner to continue his business of serving flavoured hookahs in their coffee shops without any hindrance or restrictions except under law and pass other order or orders may deem fit and proper in the circumstances of the case." 2.
texts.arguments: Sri Kuruva Naganna, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has a licence to carry out the business of running the coffee shop / restaurant and as a part of the business, the petitioner also offers hookah pot to the customers subject to satisfaction that the visiting customers are above 18 years of age, by taking a photocopy of the proof as evidence to that effect. It is submitted that the petitioner had obtained appropriate trade licenses from competent authority. It is also submitted that pursuant to the directions of the Apex Court, separate smoking area has been earmarked in the coffee shop exclusively for smoking hookah. Learned counsel submits that as per Section 4 of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003, the petitioner restaurant has seating capacity of more than 30 persons, hence, a separate provision for smoking area is provided. He submits that Respondents 3 ad 4 are frequently interfering with the business activity of serving hookah in the designated smoking area in the restaurant and preventing the petitioner from doing trade. It is also submitted that the action of the respondents in asking them to stop offering hookah in the absence of any material to show that the business is in violation of the guidelines prescribed by the Apex Court in Civil Appeal No. 10836 of 2014 arising out of SLP (Civil) No. 30832 of 2011 in Narinder S. Chadha v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai and the Cigarettes and other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution Act, 2003 (for short, 'the Act') amounts to R. Nikhil vs The State Of Telengana Rep. By Its ... on 26 December, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97944124/ 1 infringement of fundamental rights and the same is illegal and improper. Learned counsel submits that in number of writ petitions from 2014 onwards, this Court has clearly in unambiguous terms stated that the police under the guise of implementing the regulation shall not resort to cause inconvenience or any harassment to the customer / person present there or to the owner of the restaurant, when the business is lawful and legal, there cannot be any prohibition. It is also submitted that the petitioner is holding all the required licenses such as GST, Sales Tax, Food, Trade, Labour etcetera and also paid advance tax. Learned counsel submits that continuous interference of the respondents is causing irreparable damage and harassment to the petitioner and to the reputation of business. He has drawn attention of the Court to all the permissions granted by the different authorities right from Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, trade licence and the Labour Department Registration. Learned counsel also relied on the order passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in Writ Petition No. 25439 of 2018 wherein relying on the order passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Narinder S Chadha v Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai , it has been held that " I am also fortified in my view in the light of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Narinder S. Chadha's case (supra) and the amendment brought in Rule 4(3) of the Rules cannot make any difference. This Court has all the concern for the protection of the health of the adolescents falling prey to this menace of smoking tobacco products in whatever form, but so long as tobacco products, which includes hookah tobacco and consumption thereof is permitted in smoking zone as per the provision to Section 4 of the Act, use of such a tobacco product by persons above the age of 18 years, in a space provided for that purpose cannot be stopped unless and until the law circumscribes and prohibits such consumption of hookah tobacco in the smoking zones." Learned counsel submits that the respondents cannot interfere with the business of the petitioner in view of the law laid down by this Court which was fortified by the order of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Narinder S Chadha's case (supra). He submits that this Court passed interim direction in Writ Petition No. 6888 of 2014 and the petitioner is ready to comply with all the observations made therein. 3. Learned Government Pleader for Home Sri Srikanth Reddy submits that under the shadow of enabling proviso to Section 4 of the Act which says that a specific place for smokers may be provided, most of them is converting the nature of such restaurants as a place for the purpose of hookah only while allowing the youngsters to smoke hookah. If the restaurants are converted as a place for the purpose of smoking hookah, certainly licensing authority and the police have ample power to enquire into the same. It is stated that contrary to the purpose of running restaurants, if the persons are allowed only for the purpose of smoking hookah in the restaurants, the respondents have a right to cancel the licence also. It is submitted that the petitioner cannot serve hookah in the restaurants without complying with the provisions of the Act and the Rules and without displaying statutory and pictorial warnings and notices, and it amounts to violation as pointed out by the police. Further, it is stated that as per the provisions of Section 12 of the COTP Act which confers powers to the police not below the rank of Sub-Inspector of Police or any officer of the State Food or Drug Administration or any other officer, holding the equivalent rank being not below the rank of Sub-Inspector of Police authorised by the Central Government or by the State Government, may, if he has any reason to suspect that any provision of this Act has been or is being contravened, enter R. Nikhil vs The State Of Telengana Rep. By Its ... on 26 December, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97944124/ 2 and search in the manner prescribed at any reasonable time at factory, building, business or any other place. It is stated that tobacco is one of the major public health hazards and it is responsible directly or indirectly for an estimated 8 lakh deaths annually in the country and also the treatment of tobacco- related diseases and their loss of productivity cause the country much more than all the benefits recurring in the form of revenue and employment generated by tobacco industry. It is stated that basing on the recommendation made by the Parliamentary Committee, a Bill was introduced in the Parliament for a comprehensive legislation to prohibit advertising and regulation of production, supply and distribution of cigarettes and tobacco products. It is stated that as per Section 4, generally smoking in public places is prohibited, provided that in a hotel having 30 rooms or a restaurant having seating capacity of 30 persons are more and in the airports a separate provision for smoking area or space may be made. It is stated that there is a prohibition under Section 6 of the Act on sale of cigarette or other tobacco products to a person below the age of 18 years and Section 7 restricts trade and commerce in and production, supply and distribution of, cigarettes and other tobacco products. It is also stated that under Section 12, police have power to enter and search and under Section 13, the police have power to seize. It is stated that Section 29 protects the action taken by the officers in good faith. It is submitted by the learned Government Pleader that it is the bounden duty of the police to curb illegal activities, otherwise there is every chance of spoiling the bright career of the adolescent students / youth including young girls by falling prey to drug addiction. It is submitted that no instructions or circulars whatsoever were issued by the 2nd respondent regarding closure of hookah business in Hyderabad city. It is submitted that whenever the respondent police received any information regarding unlawful activities in hookah centres, the respondents are visiting the centres. Learned Government Pleader submits that as per Sections 21 and 76 of the City Police Act, the police are filing petty case charge sheets before the Court concerned. He submits that in Writ Petition No. 14192 of 2011 and batch, dated 01.07.2015, while disposing of the Writ Petition, this Court has observed as under: " The police authorities would be at liberty to regulate the business undertaken by the petitioners relating to serving of flavoured hookahs in their establishments. In terms of such regulation, it would be open to the police authorities to enter upon and cause inspection of the petitioners' business establishments for the purpose of securing due compliance with the guidelines already prescribed and also guidelines that may be prescribed in future in this regard." Learned Government Pleader submits that the petitioner is relying on the order passed by this Court in Writ Petition No. 25439 of 2018. He submits that even as per the orders passed by this Court in several Writ Petitions, the police authorities will be at liberty to regulate the business undertaken by the persons who are running Hookah parlours relating to serving fortified hookah in their establishment. In view of the same, it is always open to the police authorities to cause inspection of the business establishments for the purpose of securing true compliance of the guidelines already prescribed and the guidelines to be prescribed in future. He submits that as and when police receive any information with regard to any activity that has been carried out in hookah parlours, contrary to R. Nikhil vs The State Of Telengana Rep. By Its ... on 26 December, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97944124/ 3 the guidelines issued, it is always open to the police to inspect the premises that the respondents cannot claim it to be interference with their business. He submits that most of the school and college-going children are visiting hookah parlours and they are becoming drug addicts. He further submits that a duty is cast upon the police department to monitor these activities. Hence, he submits that only in the interest of the public at large, the police have been monitoring the same and at any cost, it cannot be termed as 'interference'. 4. Having heard learned counsel on either side, perused the material available on record. 5. 6. Though the Act does not contemplate any licence to be taken, in the larger interest of the youngsters, who are visiting the hookah centres, the restaurant owners shall have a definite place for hookah / smoking.
